title: Husayn, from me
hookLine: the younger grandson: Husayn is from me and I am from Husayn (Tirmidhi)

lines: A BOY PLAYING IN THE LANE.
HE CATCHES HIM, AND KISSES HIM.
cards: A group of companions is walking to a meal they've been invited to. Up ahead, in the lane, a little boy is playing.

The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, sees him and walks out in front of everyone with his arms wide open. The boy darts this way, then that way. The Prophet follows him, making him laugh, until he catches him.
Then he holds the boy's chin in one hand, the back of his head in the other, and kisses him, with the companions watching. The boy is Husayn. Today: what his grandfather said next.

teach.b: The companion who tells this, Ya'la ibn Murrah, remembered the words that followed, and they're kept in the collection of al-Tirmidhi.
Husayn is from me, and I am from Husayn. God loves whoever loves Husayn. Look at the order of that first sentence.
Husayn is from me: a grandson comes from his grandfather. Then it turns around. I am from Husayn, as if the grandfather, too, belongs to the child.

Muslim commentators have explained the line in more than one way: some as pure closeness, two people who can't be pulled apart; others, especially in Shi'a teaching, as a sign that the Prophet's message would be carried on through Husayn.
Either way, it's said out loud, in the street, with the companions listening. Another report, in Bukhari, sets a different habit beside it.
The Prophet kissed his grandson Hasan, and a chief named al-Aqra' ibn Habis, sitting there, said: I have ten children, and I have never kissed one of them.
The Prophet looked at him and said: whoever does not show mercy will not be shown mercy.
A leader of the community, chasing a small boy through a lane, then saying in front of everyone: this child is from me, and I am from him.
Husayn grew up, and his life ended at Karbala; Muslims, Shi'a Muslims in particular, mourn him there, and that is a story for its own day. Today belongs to the boy in the lane, laughing, caught.

how: Muslims honor Husayn as the Prophet's beloved grandson; Twelver Shi'a Muslims count him as the third Imam and mourn his death at Karbala in gatherings during the month of Muharram, especially on Ashura.

games.q: you're walking with the companions to a meal, and you see your little grandson playing in the lane. what do you do?
o: nod to him and keep walking with the men.
send someone to take him home.
go after him with open arms until you catch him.
games.why: he went out in front of everyone, chased the boy until he laughed, caught him, and kissed him, then said: Husayn is from me.

practice: Bring to mind a child, your own, a niece or nephew, a neighbor's kid, or the child you were, running in a lane.

In your mind, open your arms, go after them, let them laugh, and say silently what he said: you are from me, and I am from you. If you pray, ask God's mercy for that child; if not, just hold them close in your mind.
